story.iWant: the app to have complete PWA metadata
story.soThat: it can be installed on any device with proper branding and behavior
story.tasks:
- Task 1: Review and update manifest.ts configuration (AC: All metadata fields) - Verify `app/manifest.ts` exists (created in Story 1.4) - Update manifest to include all required fields per tech spec - Set name: "Will It Rain?" - Set short_name: "Will It Rain" - Set description: "Get a simple yes or no answer for the next 24 hours" - Set start_url: "/" - Set display: "standalone" - Set background_color: "#ffffff" - Set theme_color: "#000000" (match app color scheme) - Set orientation: "portrait-primary" or "any" - Set scope: "/" (optional, default behavior)
- Task 2: Configure PWA icons (AC: Icons array includes all required sizes) - Generate or verify icon-192.png exists in public/icons/ - Generate or verify icon-512.png exists in public/icons/ - Generate maskable-icon.png (512x512 with safe zone) in public/icons/ - Add icons array to manifest.ts with all three icons - Set purpose: "any" for icon-192 and icon-512 - Set purpose: "maskable" for maskable-icon (Android adaptive icons) - Ensure all icon paths are correct (/icons/icon-192.png, etc.)
- Task 3: Configure iOS-specific PWA meta tags (AC: iOS Add to Home Screen support) - Update app/layout.tsx metadata object - Add appleWebApp.capable: true (enable full-screen mode) - Add appleWebApp.statusBarStyle: "default" (or "black"/"black-translucent") - Add appleWebApp.title: "Will It Rain?" - Add icons.apple: "/icons/apple-touch-icon.png" (180x180 for iOS) - Generate apple-touch-icon.png (180x180) in public/icons/
- Task 4: Validate PWA manifest (AC: Manifest validates with no errors) - Run Lighthouse PWA audit in Chrome DevTools - Verify manifest serves correctly at /manifest.json - Check for validation errors in Chrome DevTools → Application → Manifest - Verify all icon paths resolve correctly - Ensure manifest meets PWA installability criteria - Test manifest validation passes with score improvements
- Task 5: Test manifest on multiple platforms (AC: Complete metadata) - Test manifest display in Chrome DevTools → Application → Manifest - Verify icon display in installability preview - Check theme_color applies to browser chrome (mobile) - Test start_url loads correctly when installed app opens - Verify display: "standalone" removes browser UI (test after install in Story 4.6)

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: **Given** the basic PWA manifest exists from Story 1.4 **When** I complete the PWA configuration **Then** manifest includes complete metadata (name, short_name, description, start_url) **And** display mode is set to "standalone" (no browser chrome) **And** theme_color and background_color are defined **And** icons array includes all required sizes (192x192, 512x512, maskable icons) **And** orientation is set appropriately (any or portrait-primary) **And** scope and start_url are correctly configured **And** manifest validates with no errors in PWA tools

Component framework, no direct PWA involvement but required for Next.js
Type safety for manifest.ts function signature (MetadataRoute.Manifest type)

constraints.constraint: Next.js Native PWA Support: Use Next.js 15+ native manifest.ts API (no next-pwa plugin needed for manifest). Manifest file must export default function returning MetadataRoute.Manifest type. Next.js automatically serves manifest at /manifest.json and links in HTML head.

No Breaking Changes: DO NOT modify API client (lib/api-client.ts), types (types/api.ts), or any Epic 3 frontend components. PWA features are additive - must preserve existing functionality from Epic 3 (frontend-backend integration).

Stateless Architecture (ADR-002): No localStorage or sessionStorage for PWA state. Service worker (Story 4.2) will cache static assets only, never API responses. Maintain stateless design principle from architecture.

Dark Mode Color Scheme: Current implementation uses #0a0a0a (near black) for background and theme colors. Tech spec suggests #ffffff for background_color and #000000 for theme_color. Verify with UX design and architecture docs before changing - may need to align colors with dark mode glassmorphic theme.

Icon Requirements: Icons already exist from Story 1.4. Verify they meet PWA requirements: 192x192 and 512x512 for Android, maskable icon with safe zone compliance (content within inner 80% circle), legible at small sizes, high contrast for visibility. If icons fail validation, may need regeneration.

iOS Apple Touch Icon: Must create apple-touch-icon.png (180x180) in public/icons/ directory. iOS requires specific icon size (180x180) separate from Android icons. Reference this in layout.tsx metadata.icons.apple property.
Naming Convention: Manifest name should be "Will It Rain?" (with question mark) per PRD branding. Short_name can be "Will It Rain" (without question mark) for space constraints on home screens.

Testing Strategy: Use Chrome DevTools → Application → Manifest to validate. Run Lighthouse PWA audit to verify installability criteria. Test on real devices (iOS, Android) after deployment to verify icons and behavior. Story 4.6 will test full installation flow.

tests.standards: Manual testing and validation for PWA manifest configuration. Use Chrome DevTools → Application → Manifest tab to inspect manifest fields and icon rendering. Run Lighthouse PWA audit (target score improvements toward 100/100). Verify manifest.json serves correctly at /manifest.json route. Test on real iOS device for apple-touch-icon display and Add to Home Screen flow. No automated unit tests required for manifest configuration (static metadata). Story 4.6 will include full installation testing across platforms.
tests.locations: Manual testing: Chrome DevTools → Application → Manifest Lighthouse audit: Chrome DevTools → Lighthouse → Progressive Web App category Manifest validation: /manifest.json route in browser iOS testing: Real iPhone device or simulator (Add to Home Screen)

ideas.test: Test: Verify manifest includes all required fields Steps: Open Chrome DevTools → Application → Manifest, verify name, short_name, description, start_url, display, background_color, theme_color, orientation all present with correct values Expected: All fields display in Manifest panel with no errors or warnings

Test: Verify icons array includes all required sizes Steps: Check Manifest panel icons section, verify 192x192, 512x512, and maskable 512x512 icons listed and render correctly Expected: Three icons display in preview, no broken image errors, sizes match specifications

Test: Verify manifest validates with no errors Steps: Run Lighthouse PWA audit, check for manifest-related errors or warnings Expected: No manifest validation errors, PWA installability criteria improvements (may not fully pass until Story 4.2 service worker is complete)

Test: Verify iOS meta tags are present Steps: View page source in Safari, search for apple-web-app-capable, apple-web-app-status-bar-style, apple-web-app-title, apple-touch-icon meta tags Expected: All four iOS-specific meta tags present in HTML head with correct values

Test: Verify theme_color applies to browser chrome Steps: Open app in Chrome Mobile (Android), observe address bar color Expected: Address bar color matches theme_color from manifest (should be dark to align with app theme)
